NDT training near Farmington: Four Corners routes into inspection, from assistant jobs to online study

The San Juan Basin keeps inspection crews busy, but someone in Farmington searching "NDT classes near me" will not find a local NDT school. In our review of college listings for this page we found no NDT certificate in the Four Corners area. The realistic routes are an assistant job with an inspection company in town, a college programme several hundred miles away, or online theory with the practical done for an employer. Each suits a different person, so start by being clear about where you stand.

Who offers NDT training around Farmington?

  • Inspection companies in Farmington. Acuren has advertised an NDT assistant role in Farmington: setting up equipment, helping radiographers calibrate it, assisting with tests, recording results and carrying gear. It asked for a high school diploma, a background check, a TWIC card or the ability to obtain one, and local residence, and preferred the 40-hour radiation safety course and a state radiographer card or trainee status. Assistant roles like this are the usual way into the trade in the basin.
  • Weld and pressure-equipment inspection. The same company has advertised a long-term CWI inspector project in Farmington on petrochemical pressure equipment, asking for a valid CWI, six years of experience and knowledge of API 510 and 570 and ASME, with API inspector certification preferred. It shows where an inspection career in the region can lead after years of method work.
  • Nearest dedicated NDT programmes. The closest we verified are in northern Utah, at Salt Lake Community College (an NDT Technology degree) and Ogden-Weber Technical College (a 32-credit non-destructive inspection programme), and in the Texas Panhandle at Amarillo College. Each is a relocation, not a commute.
  • Regional colleges. Community colleges in the region teach welding and industrial trades. If NDT is the reason you would enrol, check whether a programme actually includes an NDT introduction before you sign up. A welding certificate is still a useful base for later weld inspection work, because it teaches how defects form.

Which Farmington route fits you?

Your circumstancesRoute that suits the San Juan BasinGet clear on
Newcomer living in FarmingtonApply for an assistant role, adding a 40-hour radiation safety course if radiography crews interest youWhether the employer logs on-the-job training toward Level I
Assistant aiming at Level IIOnline theory for UT or MT plus a practical with your employerThat your hours by method match the written practice
Welder or inspector aiming at weld inspectionNDT methods together with the AWS CWIThe years of experience AWS asks for before the CWI exam
Midstream or gas processing contractor certifying staffTraining and Level III examinations at your own facilityOperator qualification and contractor-audit requirements

How a Farmington assistant usually moves up

  1. Get hired as an assistant and keep a signed log from the day you begin, listing method, task and hours.
  2. Take the 40-hour radiation safety course early if you are placed with radiography crews, because many basin postings prefer it.
  3. Complete classroom training for one method, often visual or ultrasonic thickness work, to the hours your employer's written practice sets.
  4. Sit the general, specific and practical examinations your employer's Level III administers, plus the vision test.
  5. Receive Level I certification from the employer, keep logging experience, and repeat the cycle for Level II and for further methods.

Questions to ask any NDT training provider serving the San Juan Basin

  • What will you actually scan in practice: gathering-line welds, corroded pipe and compressor parts, or reference blocks only?
  • Do the course hours meet the SNT-TC-1A recommendations for your method and level, and does the record list them in writing?
  • Who will certify you once the course ends: your employer under its written practice, or ASNT after its own exams?
  • Which Level III answers your questions during the course, and who grades the practical?
  • Can the course be completed around field work and travel, or does it need weeks away from the job?

Where Atlantis fits for Farmington candidates and employers

The Atlantis route was designed for places where no NDT school is close, and Atlantis has no classroom in the Four Corners. Method theory is online and self-paced from the day you enrol, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, so an assistant can study between jobs. You practise in the Practical NDT simulator, then complete the hands-on practical and practical exam with your employer, under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, and the employer certifies you. For basin work, visual testing and ultrasonic testing usually come before magnetic particle testing; newcomers start with NDT Level 1 training.

If the weld-inspection path appeals, the six-day AWS CWI exam preparation course runs online, one-to-one, or at an employer's facility; AWS administers the exam and certifies. Contractors in the basin can ask for a quote to have a crew trained at their own site. Nearby pages: NDT training in Albuquerque and New Mexico.
